Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Isoformic 0.2.0 (Development Version)

Release Date: Unreleased

Development Changelog: dev

This release rebuilds the package around the IsoformicExperiment class. Table-based helpers remain available as data-frame methods, but every analysis and plot is now first a method on the object.

Added

  • IsoformicExperiment is an S7 class modelled after SummarizedExperiment with three consistent levels: transcript assays, gene assays (derived by summing isoforms, cached, overridable with gene_assays<-) and exon structures from the annotation. Properties are validated on every change.
  • Annotation is stored on disk as a directory of Parquet files written by DuckDB (prepare_isoformic_annotation(), with n_exons, tx_length, metadata and sequence region tables). The parser is vocabulary-agnostic: besides GENCODE GFF3/GTF it reads Ensembl and Ensembl Rapid Release GFF3, NCBI RefSeq GFF3 and the T2T-CHM13 Liftoff/CAT annotations, keeping the source_gene/source_transcript attributes of lifted annotations as source_gene_id/source_transcript_id columns.
  • download_reference() covers Ensembl (any release, species and division, including Ensembl Plants/Metazoa/Fungi/Protists), any NCBI assembly by accession, T2T-CHM13v2.0 (reference = "t2t") and MANE releases; download_reference_url() caches any file by URL and download_hprc_annotation() fetches the HPRC per-haplotype CAT annotations.
  • Annotation tables carry transcript tags and an is_canonical flag (MANE Select, Ensembl canonical, RefSeq Select), used by dominant_isoform() to report dominant_is_canonical.
  • Haplotype-resolved annotations: prepare_isoformic_annotation(haplotype = ) labels one haplotype, merge_annotations() combines per-haplotype files (HPRC CAT, trio-binned assemblies) into one annotation directory with unique identifiers, and haplotype_summary() reports per-gene haplotype fractions and dominant-isoform switches between haplotypes.
  • FANTOM CAT / FANTOM6 support: download_reference(reference = "fantom") fetches a FANTOM CAT level (GTF), download_fantom_cat_tables() the companion tables, and the parser keeps geneClass (as gene and fallback transcript type), geneCategory, DHS_type, coding_status, cumulative_support and TIEScore; add_fantom_cat_tables() attaches CAGE cluster promoters and the gene information table.
  • Per-transcript structure: the parser aggregates CDS features (cds_start, cds_end, cds_length) and keeps transcript_support_level; transcript_features() computes ORF and UTR lengths, the 50-nt NMD rule (stop_to_last_junction, nmd_predicted), transcription start/end groups (alternative promoters and 3’ ends), the canonical isoform of each gene and splicing events relative to it (splicing_events(): skipped and novel exons, retained introns, alternative splice sites, first and last exons).
  • Productivity as a graded, computed property: transcript_productivity() (productive, altered_productive, unproductive, noncoding, uncertain, with the reason for each call), productive_fraction() per sample or group with the between-group change, run_productivity_enrichment() (gene sets ranked by change in productive fraction), poison_exons() and highlight_poison_exons in plot_genomic_context().
  • add_annotation_columns() attaches external per-transcript or per-gene evidence (Ribo-seq, NMD inhibition, GTEx dominant isoforms, domain retention, …) to the annotation; a productivity_evidence column overrides the computed productivity.
  • Transcript sequences: extract_transcript_sequences() stores the spliced sequence of every transcript in the annotation directory (annot_data_sequences.parquet), from a genome FASTA (streamed in chunks, gzip or plain, chromosome names matched with or without chr) or a transcript FASTA; has_sequences() and transcript_sequences() read it.
  • Sequence-aware ORFs: transcript_orfs() projects the canonical start codon of each gene onto every isoform and translates it (the ORFanage approach), so novel transcripts without CDS get an ORF; annotated CDS are re-read from the sequence (annotation_cds_agrees), with stop codon, genomic coordinates, uORFs, frame relative to the canonical ORF and an NMD class (ptc, ptc_start_proximal, non_stop, long_3utr, none). coding_potential() scores the longest ORF with the Fickett statistic, an in-frame hexamer score and a frozen logistic model trained on GENCODE 49 (build_coding_model(), data-raw/build_coding_model.R; held-out sensitivity 0.96, specificity 0.93).
  • transcript_productivity() uses the sequence-derived ORFs when present (use_sequence), reports source (sequence, annotation, evidence), distinguishes alternative starts, in-frame changes, frameshifts and stops in novel sequence among altered_productive isoforms, calls non-stop decay and start-proximal stops, and applies evidence columns in a fixed priority (productivity_evidence, validated NMD exon, Ribo-seq main ORF, APPRIS principal).
  • Frozen evidence datasets (frozen_datasets(), fetch_frozen_data(), read_frozen_data(), build_frozen_*()): APPRIS principal isoforms and method scores plus SPADE Pfam domain coordinates (e113v49), GENCODE Ribo-seq ORFs phase 1 and 2, NMD-inducing exons validated by NMD inhibition (Karousis et al. 2021), the PolyASite 2.0 atlas and GTEx v8 median transcript TPM per tissue. Files are pinned by version and MD5, downloaded from the first mirror that has them (frozen_mirrors(): user option, the frozen-data GitHub release, the Zenodo snapshot of the processed files) or rebuilt from the sources; bundle_frozen_data() assembles the Zenodo deposit and data-raw/README.md documents the update and deposit procedure.
  • New article “What makes an isoform hard to quantify?”: three samples quantified with 30 and 100 Gibbs draws, and how transcript type, reads, length, exons, isoforms in the gene, GC content, MANE and support tags, NAGNAG and nearby alternative splice sites, unique exonic bases, the closest sibling and unique fragments relate to the inferential uncertainty, to how reliably 30 draws measure it, and to the stability of TreeTerminus trees. The tables come from data-raw/knockdown/isoform_features.R and ship in inst/extdata/knockdown/stability/.
  • read_treeterminus() reads the transcript trees of TreeTerminus (Newick; leaves are positions in quant.sf, named from a Salmon directory) and cut_transcript_trees() cuts them where the inferential relative variance of the summed replicates falls below the cutoff: an isoform the reads determine stays itself, one they do not is replaced by its lowest well-determined ancestor, and nested choices are merged so that the groups never overlap. The groups go to add_uncertainty(groups = ), so the confidence classes and collapse_groups work at the resolution the data support, isoform by isoform. Tested on real TreeTerminus output.
  • run_terminus() runs Terminus from R (terminus group on every Salmon directory, then the consensus terminus collapse) through condathis, checks first that every directory has replicates and equivalence-class weights, deletes the multi-gigabyte delta.log of each sample as soon as it is grouped, and returns the consensus groups. On the six GSE129540 samples it reproduces the consensus of the command-line run.
  • read_terminus_groups() reads the transcript groups of Terminus (terminus collapse, clusters.txt), and add_uncertainty(groups = ) accepts them (or any table of transcript_id and group_id) in place of the groups built from the correlation of the replicates; the confidence classes, collapse_groups and uncertainty_methods() follow the new groups. The parser is tested on real output of Terminus 0.1.0 on Salmon 2.8.0.
  • test_usage() tests differential transcript usage with edgeR diffSplice, satuRn or DEXSeq (all in Suggests) on counts divided by the overdispersion of the replicates, and reports transcript and gene level p-values in one layout. With more than two groups it tests every level against the first, every pair (contrasts = "pairwise") or a list of c(numerator, denominator) pairs, and stacks the results with a contrast column; diffSplice and satuRn fit all groups once, DEXSeq fits each pair. contrasts = "omnibus" tests for a difference among any of the groups: the DEXSeq likelihood-ratio test on all samples, or the Simes combination of the contrasts against the reference for diffSplice and satuRn.
  • read_oarfish_sc() reads the single-cell output of Oarfish (--single-cell: .count.mtx, .barcodes.txt, .features.txt) and sums the cells of each sample, given a table of barcodes and samples, into an IsoformicExperiment (pseudobulk; TPM from the annotated transcript lengths). read_oarfish_sc_counts() returns the cell-level counts as a long table. The fixture is real Oarfish 0.10.3 output on simulated barcoded reads.
  • read_oarfish() reads long-read quantifications from Oarfish (counts, lengths, TPM computed from them). read_inferential_replicates(), equivalence_support() (from the unique and ambiguous read counts), salmon_run_qc() and add_uncertainty() accept Oarfish output prefixes, including the Parquet bootstrap replicates (.infreps.pq). The bundled fixture is real Oarfish 0.10.3 output on simulated nanopore reads. Mixing Oarfish and Salmon in one call is an error (isoformic_mixed_quantifiers).
  • inferential_overdispersion() and scale_counts() put the quantification uncertainty into the counts as edgeR::catchSalmon() does (Baldoni et al. 2024), from the replicates stored in the object; the estimates match catchSalmon() on a full 517,038-transcript quantification. A read-split experiment on GSE129540 (data-raw/knockdown/validate_uncertainty.R) backs the confidence classes: of the isoforms that are large and stable over the draws in null contrasts, almost none are classed high, and the isoforms called in one half of the reads reproduce in the other half less often as the class or the inferential variance worsens. The small result tables are bundled and shown in the uncertainty article.
  • Fixes from a code review: write_isoformic(overwrite = TRUE) writes to a sibling directory and swaps it in, so overwriting the directory an object was read from no longer deletes it (and refuses directories that are not experiments, isoformic_not_experiment_dir); de_table() and plot_log2fc() accept results that already have gene_name, gene_id or transcript_name columns; test_productive_fraction() and test_apa() contrast two of several groups with levels; join_DEG_DET() uses the same cutoff rule as the stored cutoffs (>= and <=) and gains use_fdr; a frozen dataset that fails its checksum after download is discarded and the next mirror is tried; plot_log2fc() no longer drops its title when a requested feature has no data; the assay hash behind the caches is computed once when the assays are set; tools is declared in Imports.
  • Inferential replicates convert to and from a long table (inferential_replicates_table(), as_inferential_replicates()), and the bundled draws are Parquet tables instead of .rds files.
  • Real ESRP knockdown examples for the uncertainty article: GSE129540 (prostate cancer, ESRP2 siRNA) and GSE75489 (H358 cells, ESRP1/2 shRNA), re-quantified with Salmon 2.8.0 and 30 Gibbs draws, reduced to 41 genes (under 1 MB). data-raw/knockdown/quantify_knockdown.sh and data-raw/build_knockdown_example.R rebuild them. add_uncertainty() scales the counts with the library_size column of col_data() when present (for objects holding a subset of the transcripts) and accepts the table of equivalence_support() in equivalence.
  • Quantification uncertainty from Salmon: read_inferential_replicates(), equivalence_support() and salmon_run_qc() read the Gibbs/bootstrap replicates, the equivalence classes and the run metadata; add_uncertainty() (or read_salmon(inferential = TRUE)) stores, per transcript, the inferential relative variance, the correlation with the isoforms of the same gene (ambiguity groups that cannot be told apart) and the share of uniquely mapping fragments. de_confidence() repeats a contrast on every draw and reports the interval and sign agreement of the fold-change with a high/moderate/low confidence class, optionally testing ambiguous isoforms as one feature. uncertainty_report() and uncertainty_methods() summarise the results and the settings for a manuscript; plot_de_confidence(), plot_isoform_correlation() and plot_inf_rv() draw them. isoform_switches(confident_only = TRUE), dominant_isoform() and productive_fraction() use them. The tables are written by write_isoformic(); the draws stay in memory.
  • salmon_quant() draws 30 Gibbs samples by default (it was 100; num_gibbs = 0 skips them).
  • salmon_index() and salmon_quant() target Salmon 2 (the Rust rewrite; the conda environment installs 2.8.0): options that Salmon 2 ignores (--no-version-check, --type puff, --disableChainingHeuristic, --useVBOpt) are no longer passed, single-end reads are passed with --unmatedReads, and the documentation explains that indices built with Salmon 1.x must be rebuilt.
  • The documentation site is split into an introduction, a preprocessing article and one article per analysis (diversity, productivity, polyadenylation, enrichment, plots), plus articles on other annotations and on the table-based functions.
  • ?isoformic-options documents every option and environment variable the package reads or is affected by: the isoformic.frozen_mirrors option, the base R download options, the cache location variables and the settings of DuckDB and condathis.
  • Evidence joins: add_appris(), add_riboseq_orfs() (listed transcripts and exon-block compatibility, riboseq_main_orf, riboseq_uorf), add_nmd_exons(), domain_retention() (domains retained, partial or lost relative to the canonical isoform, projected onto novel isoforms) and gtex_reference() / gtex_tissues() (healthy-tissue productive fraction and dominant isoform per gene).
  • Productivity statistics: productivity_fractions() (expression share per class and unproductive mechanism: NMD, retained intron, no ORF, non-stop), test_productive_fraction() (quasi-binomial two-group test on counts), productive_fraction(min_expr = , inf_reps = , reference = ) (expression floor, uncertainty from Salmon inferential replicates, difference to the GTEx baseline), dominant_isoform(min_expr = ) and benchmark_productivity() (recall of NMD and retained-intron biotypes by the rules alone, productive rate of coding and canonical transcripts).
  • Alternative polyadenylation: polya_sites() ranks the 3’ ends of each gene, classifies tandem_utr, alternative_last_exon and intronic events relative to the canonical isoform, finds poly(A) signal hexamers in the sequence and validates ends against the PolyASite atlas or the GENCODE poly(A) GFF (download_reference(file_type = "polya"), read_polya_gff()); apa_usage() quantifies distal usage and weighted 3’ UTR length per sample or group and test_apa() tests the shift.
  • Long-read and assembled transcript catalogs: StringTie/Bambu/FLAIR style GTF attributes (reference_id, ref_gene_id, ref_gene_name) are kept, and add_sqanti_classification() writes SQANTI3 structural categories into transcript_type; tx_type_palette() includes those categories and the unknown/novel labels. Tables are read on first use and cached keyed by file signature, so objects sharing an annotation share one copy.
  • Experiments persist as Parquet directories: write_isoformic() and read_isoformic() (optionally self-contained with copy_annotation = TRUE).
  • Readers: read_salmon() reads quant.sf files straight into an IsoformicExperiment with DuckDB; read_parquet(), write_parquet() and read_tabular() are exported; make_tx_to_gene() parses FASTA headers with DuckDB and also accepts GFF3/GTF files and annotation directories.
  • SummarizedExperiment-style accessors: assays(), assay(), assay<-, assay_names(), gene_assays(), gene_assay(), gene_data(), gene_names(), row_names(), col_names(), col_data<-, exon_table(), annot_metadata(), clear_cache(), plus dim(), dimnames() and [.
  • Differential expression results are standardised on assignment (de_tx<-, de_gene<- accept DESeq2, edgeR, limma and fishpond column names) and flagged with stored cutoffs (de_cutoffs(), de_cutoffs<-, de_table()).
  • Transcriptomic diversity summaries: isoform_fraction(), tx_diversity() (expressed isoforms, dominant isoform, effective number of isoforms), dominant_isoform() (per group, with dominance switches), isoform_switches() (transcript versus gene level calls) and exon_diversity() (constitutive versus alternative exons).
  • as_summarized_experiment() converts back to SummarizedExperiment at the transcript or gene level; as_isoformic() also accepts tximport lists.
  • example_isoformic() loads a bundled experiment (preeclampsia placenta subset, GENCODE v33) used by all examples and tests.
  • profile_data() and plot_tx_expr() methods for the object; plot_enrichment() and read_gmt().
  • summarize_to_gene() is exported and sums isoforms (abundance-weighted mean for length assays, as tximport does).

Changed

  • plot_genomic_context() is a pure ggplot2 implementation reading the exon table of the annotation (one row per transcript, introns with strand arrows, expression labels and highlighted differentially expressed isoforms); it no longer needs plotgardener, txdbmaker, TxDb, OrgDb or BSgenome packages. plot_tx_context() is now an alias of its data frame method and accepts the legacy column names.
  • plot_log2fc() facets several genes, orders the gene bar first and uses a common theme; plot_log2FC() is kept as a wrapper.
  • plot_tx_expr() and run_enrichment() are S7 generics whose first argument is the object (or a table); run_enrichment() no longer takes the unused lfc_cutoff argument and expands gene sets with a single join.
  • prepare_profile_data() returns the same long table as profile_data() (feature_name, feature_type, gene_name, group, mean_expr, sd_expr, is_de); gene expression is the sum of the isoforms (it was the mean).
  • prepare_annotation() and prepare_exon_annotation() read the Parquet annotation directory and return standard column names (transcript_id, start_pos, end_pos, …).
  • Bundled example tables are now Parquet (pe_abundance.parquet, pe_det.parquet, pe_deg.parquet, pe_col_data.parquet).
  • download_reference() discovers files by listing the release directory on the server instead of relying on hard-coded file names, so any current or future GENCODE release (and genome patch, e.g. GRCh38.p15) works. New region argument ("all", "chr", "primary") selects the annotation flavour; versions are normalised (49, "v49", "38" for mouse). Errors are specific: no internet, release not found (listing the latest releases), file not found in the release (listing the candidates), and failed or empty transfers (partial files are removed). Defaults: GENCODE release 49, file_type = "gff", output_path = ":cache:".
  • Development tooling: jarl.toml (all jarl rules), a jarl-check GitHub workflow, lint and test-coverage workflows, and justfile recipes aligned with condathis.

Removed

  • ContextData, create_context_data() and prepare_annotation_db().
  • Dependencies arrow, vroom, readr, purrr, stringr, tidyr and ggpubr; suggested packages plotgardener, txdbmaker, GenomicFeatures, IRanges, AnnotationHub, org.Hs.eg.db, BSgenome.Hsapiens.NCBI.GRCh38, TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene, viridis, carrier and mirai.

Isoformic 0.1.2

Release Date: 2025-10-06

Development Changelog: 0.1.2

Added

  • New DuckDB based parse_annotation().
  • New plot_genomic_context() function to visualize the genomic context of a gene with its transcripts.
  • New tx_type_palette() function to provide a default color palette for transcript types.

Fixed

  • In make_tx_to_gene() output, wrong column name entrez_id replaced for tx_length.

Isoformic 0.1.1

Release Date: 2024-06-18

Development Changelog: 0.1.1

Added

  • download_reference(): now supports organism = c("human", "mouse"), with organism = "human" being the default.
  • download_reference(): argument file_type = "gtf" is the default.
  • prepare_annotation(): Parse both GTF and GFF file formats into required annotation data.

Fixed

  • prepare_profile_data(): accepts matrix and data.frame as input for the txi_transcript argument.
